subject: Persistent dedicated pool latency — reconciliation & next steps
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@cycloneai.com>

Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: sustained latency from dedicated pool (us-west-2) since 7/29

Hi Marissa / Naomi,

We started seeing sustained tail latency and a higher 5xx rate for our production endpoints in the dedicated pool (us-west-2) late yesterday evening (around 23:40 PDT). Throughput is stable, but median latency is OK — the problem is a long tail. This is affecting a subset of inference requests that hit longer sequences.

We've attached a short snippet of logs. Can you confirm what happened and whether this is tied to the autoscaler change you shipped last week? Our SREs are on standby and would like an ETA for a mitigation.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Platform Engineering, CycloneAI

Attachment: excerpt_error_rate_0729-0730.txt (text)

Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sustained latency from dedicated pool (us-west-2) since 7/29

Hi Emma — thank you for the heads up and the logs. I'm sorry you're seeing that impact. We're investigating immediately.

Short version: Ops is treating this as Priority 1 for CycloneAI. I'll coordinate a short call if helpful, but first pass: our release last week made a default autoscaler policy tweak to weight memory headroom more aggressively for long-sequence workloads; early telemetry suggests that for some tenanted pools that run mixed-length traffic this increased contention for warm cache slots and led to KV cache eviction churn, which amplified tail latency.

Immediate next steps I'm pushing now:
- Open a hotfix to revert the memory-headroom weight for your pool (ETA 2 hours)
- Temporarily pin your tenant to a compatible pool variant without the new policy (ETA 30–60m)
- Collect a compact RCA and proposed credit offer within 72 hours

Would you like us to schedule a 30-minute bridge with your SREs now?

—Marissa
Director, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

My read (ops): the autoscaler policy tweak we rolled last week changed the scoring so that long-sequence requests prioritized memory headroom, which in mixed-tenancy pools can cause more frequent KV cache evictions. The eviction churn looks like it created the long tail.

Proposals:
- Karthik: can your team produce the revert hotfix? Ben/Naomi: initiate customer comms and draft credit language. I'll own timeline and post-incident summary.

I've started a tracking ticket: OPS-4927. Push back if you disagree with the diagnosis.

Working on it — infra team reproduced the eviction churn on a canary using a mixed-length workload generator. Root cause looks like the new scoring function combined with a side-effect in the cache allocator when contention > 72%.

Actions completed:
- Pinned CycloneAI's tenant to pool variant v1.36 (pre-tweak) at 10:37 PDT — rollback avoided any immediate 5xx increase
- Deployed a targeted kernel-level hotfix to bypass the eviction path under high contention and started monitoring (10:52 PDT)

Next: prepare a full revert for the autoscaler policy and a controlled rollout plan (ETA for revert PR merged: 18:00 PDT today). Will document the canary results and attach to OPS-4927.

Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sustained latency from dedicated pool (us-west-2) since 7/29 — interim report and credit proposal

Hi Emma — quick status and suggested next steps.

What we did (timeline summary):
- 2027-07-30 10:37 PDT: pinned your tenant to pool variant v1.36 (pre-policy tweak) — immediate reduction in tail latency
- 2027-07-30 10:52 PDT: deployed kernel-level bypass to reduce eviction churn — stabilized error rate
- 2027-07-30 17:45 PDT: canary revert PR opened and validated for standard mixed-length workloads

Root cause (short): the autoscaler scoring tweak increased memory-headroom weight; for certain mixed-length tenanted pools this raised eviction frequency past a threshold where warm KV cache effectiveness collapsed, producing long-tail latencies and transient 5xx for a slice of requests. We've documented the sequence in OPS-4927 and attached a compact root cause summary.

Proposed remediation & customer-facing items:
1) Permanent revert of the autoscaler scoring change for mixed-tenancy pools (target: roll at low-traffic window 2027-08-03 to minimize risk)
2) Two mitigations we've backported: kernel bypass and tenant pinning as immediate fallbacks
3) Quality assurance: add mixed-length workload tests to the autoscaler job spec and increase canary run time from 2h -> 12h before rollouts

Compensation proposal: because the incident affected requests across your production pool for ~6 hours peak impact, we propose a 12% usage credit for the billing period in which the incident occurred. We'll provide a simple usage_credit_agreement for signature; legal is prepared to expedite.

Attachments: rcc_root_cause_summary.pdf (2 pages), usage_credit_agreement-CycloneAI.pdf (draft)

Would you like a brief joint exec-to-exec readout this week? Happy to coordinate.

—Marissa

Short post-incident summary (for auditors):
- Impact window (peak): 2027-07-29 23:40 PDT -> 2027-07-30 05:25 PDT (approx)
- Primary failure mode: autoscaler scoring change -> increased KV cache eviction churn under >72% contention -> long tail latency and localized 5xx
- Immediate mitigations: tenant pin to v1.36, kernel bypass; both reduced eviction churn and stabilized tail latency
- Preventive changes: revert policy for mixed-tenancy pools, expanded canary tests, longer canary duration, and an improved monitoring alert for eviction-rate regressions

- Legal will send the credit agreement for signature and apply the credit after countersignature (Ben to lead)
